questions.q: Why does a single-stage build carry "dead weight" into production for Northbridge's React-based catalog frontend?
options: Because single-stage builds are slower to run, not larger
Because the final image still contains the full Node toolchain, dev dependencies, and unbuilt source, even though the running app only needs the compiled static output
Because single-stage Dockerfiles cannot use EXPOSE
Because React apps cannot be containerized with a single stage at all
questions.explain: Everything used to build the app -- the compiler, bundler, dev dependencies, source files -- is unnecessary once the static output (dist/) exists, but a single-stage build ships it all anyway.

questions.q: What does `FROM node:20 AS build` do in a multi-stage Dockerfile?
options: It deletes the previous stage entirely
It names this stage "build" so a later stage can reference it with COPY --from=build
It tells Docker to only build this stage and skip the rest of the file
It sets the final image's tag to "build"
questions.explain: The AS clause gives a build stage a name, which a later COPY --from=<name> instruction can reference to pull specific files out of it.

options: It copies the entire build stage, including node_modules and source files, into the final image
It copies only the /app/dist directory from the named build stage into the current (runtime) stage -- nothing else from that stage comes along
It runs the build stage's CMD inside the runtime stage
It merges the build stage and runtime stage into a single combined image
questions.explain: COPY --from=<stage> pulls only the specified path out of that earlier stage. None of the build stage's other files, tools, or layers make it into the final image.

questions.q: Why does the runtime stage in the Northbridge example use `FROM nginx:1.27-alpine` instead of continuing with `node:20`?
options: nginx is required by Docker for any multi-stage build
The running app is just static files to serve, so a minimal web server image is sufficient and far smaller than carrying the full Node toolchain
node:20 cannot be used as a runtime stage under any circumstances
nginx automatically compiles TypeScript at runtime
questions.explain: Once the app is built to static HTML/JS/CSS, serving it needs nothing more than a lightweight web server -- there's no reason to carry Node and its toolchain into the shipped image.

questions.q: In the Northbridge example, the build stage still runs `npm install` and `npm run build` in full. Why doesn't that weight end up in the final image?
options: Docker automatically deletes node_modules after every build regardless of stage
Because only the files explicitly copied out with COPY --from=build make it into the final image -- the rest of the build stage is discarded
Because npm install and npm run build don't actually create any files
Because the build stage and runtime stage share the same filesystem automatically
questions.explain: Each stage is isolated. The build stage's layers (node_modules, source, compiler) only exist within that stage; the final image is built fresh from the runtime stage's FROM, plus whatever is explicitly copied in.
